slides.headline: She gives him one thing to take to war.
The departure
slides.text: A knight in armour is riding out to war. On the castle steps, the lady he loves leans down to say goodbye.

slides.headline: The scarf
slides.text: She ties a red scarf around his arm. In the age of chivalry, a lady's favour was both a promise and a protection.

slides.headline: His face
slides.text: He looks up at her from under the steel helmet, almost shy. A knight's armour, and a boy's tenderness in his eyes.

slides.headline: Her gown
slides.text: She wears a golden gown, her long hair loose down her back. Leighton paints her like a princess from a fairy tale.

slides.headline: The gate
slides.text: Behind them, other knights are already riding through the castle gate, banners raised. He has only a moment left.

slides.headline: The roses
slides.text: Roses climb the old stone walls around her. In Leighton's world, love always grows right next to danger.
Leighton painted this dream of knights in 1900, the same year Britain's soldiers were away fighting a real war in South Africa.

slides.headline: Let him go?
slides.text: She has given him her token. Will he come back to her? And if you were her, would you let him go?
